sonnet.problem: Card 3 already says 'the covenant of their fathers', so the word 'covenant', the right answer to this fill-in-the-blank, appears on an earlier card. A baker can pick it by recalling that word instead of reasoning.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: 'That line again' points back to 'guard yourselves in your spirit and do not break faith.' Card 15 only showed a paraphrase of it inside a question ('guard themselves in their spirit and not break faith with the wife of their youth'). The words are not an exact match and no earlier card showed them.
sonnet.rule: What he points out must be true. "Same words" means an exact match. He only points back to words a card has shown.

sonnet.problem: The joke sits on verse 14, where the people have broken faith with the wife of their youth. That is serious sin and a hurtful moment. The next card says 'I think this one hurts', but this card still carries a joke.
sonnet.rule: A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.
